findings.title: LP-02 same-key lock contention now returns the stable retryable conflict
findings.observation: The outer transaction catch now rolls back and converts PostgreSQL 55P03 into the inherited 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS result.
findings.trigger: An overlapping LP-02 request waits on the same uncommitted idempotency key beyond the two-second lock timeout.
findings.impact: Clients receive the deterministic retry-same-key signal rather than a generic 500, and the aborted attempt leaves no partial business or idempotency write.

evidence.description: The current helper performs rollback before mapping 55P03 and matches the accepted LP-01 inProgress envelope.
The database-backed route regression proves 409, rollback recovery, exact replay and one transition/audit/idempotency row.
The behavior satisfies inherited idempotency, atomic mutation and recovery requirements.

findings.remediation: Completed at the exact reviewed head.
findings.verification: Preserve the real held-key regression and all unit, contract, integration, LP-01/LP-02 acceptance and exact-head CI gates.

findings.title: Broad 55P03 mapping can imprecisely label unrelated row-lock contention
findings.observation: Because SET LOCAL lock_timeout applies to the whole transaction, the outer catch maps any 55P03—including a different-key project-row lock timeout—to IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS.
findings.trigger: A command owns a distinct idempotency key but waits more than two seconds on a project row held by another transaction.
findings.impact: The response message attributes contention to the original same-key request even when the blocked resource is a project row. Rollback occurs first, no side effect or key survives, and retrying the same key remains safe.

evidence.description: The 55P03 predicate is outside the ownership insert and covers all work(client) queries under the transaction-wide lock timeout.
A fresh-context rollback-only reproduction held validation_projects FOR UPDATE; the competing different-key request returned 409 after about 2020 ms with zero persisted idempotency rows.
After the blocker clears, same-key retry can safely execute or return the normal version conflict because the timed-out transaction was rolled back.

findings.remediation: Optionally narrow the 55P03-to-idempotency mapping to ownership acquisition or distinguish lock sources while preserving rollback and safe retry.
findings.verification: A different-key held-project-row regression should retain zero partial writes and return the intentionally chosen contention classification after the lock clears.
